cover.title: Connections and payment methods
cover.subtitle: Providers and local payment methods in Waymo's seven announced markets and across Latin America

regions.name: Asia Pacific
regions.headline: Japan, Singapore and Australia each have twenty or more providers live through Yuno, with the local wallets and konbini riders use.
regions.note: Japan: Tokyo 2027. Singapore: 2028. Australia: in talks.

regions.name: Europe and North America
regions.headline: London, Munich, Madrid and Toronto are covered by the global acquirers plus the local rails of each market.
regions.note: United Kingdom: London 2026. Germany: Munich 2027. Spain: Madrid, testing from late 2026. Canada: Toronto 2028.

regions.name: Latin America
regions.headline: Every Latin American market has live providers and its main local methods through Yuno, with redundancy in the large ones.
regions.note: All Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking markets with Yuno coverage; Cuba is not served.

markets: London: commercial service planned for 2026, timing tied to UK approval; Moove runs fleet operations
Tokyo: driverless commercial service targeted for 2027 with Nihon Kotsu and GO, subject to permits
Munich: testing from late 2026, public launch targeted for the end of 2027, federal permit pending
Madrid: Waymo Iberia SL registered, testing before the end of 2026, no launch date announced
Announced September 2026 with MOT and LTA: manual driving in 2027, ride-hailing launch in 2028 subject to approvals
Toronto: first riders targeted for 2028, Element Fleet Management runs the fleet
Talks with the federal, NSW and Victoria governments reported in January 2026; no permit application filed
markets_headline: Seven countries outside the US have a public Waymo plan today; this deck covers them plus every Latin American market.
markets_note: Public announcements as of 22 October 2026. No other country has an announced Waymo launch. Providers live = connections available through Yuno in that country.
markets_sources: Market status sources: Waymo blog (London, Oct 2025), CNBC (Munich, 25 Aug 2026), The Olive Press (Madrid, 25 Aug 2026), Fortune and LTA (Singapore, 17 Sep 2026), Element Fleet and TipRanks (Toronto, 2028), Nihon Kotsu and GO (Tokyo 2027), AFR via ACS (Australia, Jan 2026).
